recipe_title: Cozy Chicken, Mushroom, and Wild Rice Soup

details.title_candidate: Cozy Chicken, Mushroom, and Wild Rice Soup
ingredients_sketch: Pre-cooked brown and wild rice blend (ready-to-eat pouch)

warnings: Stage 4 coverage: 'Extra-virgin olive oil': [748608] Oil, olive, extra virgin has no USDA value for fiber_g, protein_g (which would be summed as zero) — switched to [171413] Oil, olive, salad or cooking.

[chapter_intent_fit] The recipe embodies a 'light main' perfectly, but barely misses the tier's guardrails (carbohydrates at 46.8g vs the 45g ceiling; fiber at 5.9g vs the 6g floor). Fix: Reduce the rice blend to 1 1/4 cups and increase the spinach to 4 cups to gently correct both numbers into the target window.

details.summary: A beautifully constructed, comforting soup that successfully utilizes a ready-to-eat grain pouch to deliver deep, simmered flavor well under the 30-minute limit, while perfectly honoring the dietary needs of both conditions.

dimensions.feedback: The earthy mushrooms, thyme, and wild rice create a classic, savory foundation, and the splash of apple cider vinegar at the end provides exactly the right amount of acidity to brighten the broth.
Every listed ingredient is cleanly and clearly accounted for in the instructions.
The steps are thoroughly written with appropriate time ranges, specific check times, and clear visual and textural doneness cues for every cooking phase.
Perfectly aligns with Classic American soup profiles, using standard, recognizable aromatics and techniques.
The one-pot simmering method is entirely appropriate for this type of quick soup, allowing the flavors to meld rapidly without drying anything out.
The computed macronutrients are accurate and reflect the ingredients provided, especially the protein from the chicken and the carbohydrates from the rice blend.
The title and intro accurately describe the dish in a warm, appealing, and practical way without relying on any banned or sensational health claims.
Highly appealing. It reads as a comforting, hearty, and highly accessible weeknight or lunch option that home cooks will actually want to make.
Delivers wonderfully for both blood sugar and the liver: leans entirely on extra-virgin olive oil, provides plenty of vegetables, features lean protein, and uses a whole, unrefined grain.
Zero added sugar, and the carbohydrate component (the brown and wild rice blend) is a high-quality, fiber-rich, whole-grain choice.

The recipe embodies a 'light main' perfectly, but barely misses the tier's guardrails (carbohydrates at 46.8g vs the 45g ceiling; fiber at 5.9g vs the 6g floor). Fix: Reduce the rice blend to 1 1/4 cups and increase the spinach to 4 cups to gently correct both numbers into the target window.

Excellent use of the pre-cooked rice pouch—a first-class shortcut that allows a traditionally slow-cooking ingredient to feature in a genuinely under-30-minute soup. The prep and cook times are realistic.
